OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $k\geq 3$ and $f_{k,3}(x)$ denote the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of three nonnegative $k$th powers. Is it true that\[f_{k,3}(x) \gg x^{3/k}\]or even $\gg_\epsilon x^{3/k-\epsilon}$? 
#325: [ErGr80]
number theory | 
powers
Mahler and Erdős [ErMa38] proved that $f_{k,2}(x) \gg x^{2/k}$. For $k=3$ the best known is due to Wooley [Wo15],\[f_{3,3}(x) \gg x^{0.917\cdots}.\]This problem has been formalised in Lean as part of the Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures project.

 Using ChatGPT Deep Research, I came across a paper which proves the statement for k≥33:
https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:1fd05b3e-cd34-4b65-a95e-590af2e523dc/files/m4c717ccd310e4b8622a4423c5dcf3075
From the corollary: "For d ≥ 33 there are asymptotically $\frac{1}{6} c x^{3/d}$ integers n ≤ x which are sums of three d-th powers".
Full deep research results: https://chatgpt.com/share/69ae2aa8-1eac-8003-b208-71fb3127bd7e
